name: hicp (CRAN mirror)
what_it_holds: Read-only GitHub mirror of the CRAN R package 'hicp' — tools to access and compute Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices data (price indices and weights) from Eurostat's public database, implementing methodology from Eurostat's 2024 HICP Methodological Manual. Built on data.table; ships functions (documented in the package vignette, not fully visible here) for aggregating/decomposing HICP series.
why_useful: An official-methodology R toolkit for pulling and re-aggregating Eurostat HICP series (including the accommodation-services / restaurants-hotels COICOP branch) with correct chain-linking, better than ad hoc pulls of the published index — useful if the team wants a defensible, reproducible EMEA accommodation-price series.
license: R package license (CRAN, likely GPL — not confirmed)
last_activity: package current as of CRAN mirror sync, references 2024 manual
time_coverage: whatever Eurostat HICP history covers (HICP monthly since 1996 varies by country)
size_hint: R package source, no large committed data
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: An official-methodology R toolkit for pulling and re-aggregating Eurostat HICP series (including the accommodation-services / restaurants-hotels COICOP branch) with correct chain-linking, better than ad hoc pulls of the published index — useful if the team wants a defensible, reproducible EMEA accommodation-price series.

name: attention-flow
what_it_holds: Active research repo (MIT, 73 commits, daily CI) using daily Wikipedia pageviews as a free 'market attention' proxy for ~34 entities/39 edges across four 2020-2026 economic-narrative graphs (AI buildout, GLP-1, EV/battery, COVID). Caches raw pageview pulls under data/raw/, trains a GRU+graph-attention network to forecast one-week-ahead 'attention shocks', and publishes live graded forecast-accuracy JSON (data.json, track.json) via a running demo.
why_useful: Not itself a tourism dataset, but a live, working, actively-updated methodological template for exactly the technique Gap 5/17 wants: turning free Wikipedia pageviews into a leading demand-attention signal with a public accuracy scoreboard and a graph/GNN structure that could be re-pointed at Airbnb/BKNG/EXPE/hotel-chain and destination-city Wikipedia pages instead of AI/pharma/EV entities.
size_hint: ~34 entities x daily pageviews since 2020, plus trained GNN checkpoints
last_activity: actively updated (daily CI as of query date)
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Not itself a tourism dataset, but a live, working, actively-updated methodological template for exactly the technique Gap 5/17 wants: turning free Wikipedia pageviews into a leading demand-attention signal with a public accuracy scoreboard and a graph/GNN structure that could be re-pointed at Airbnb/BKNG/EXPE/hotel-chain and destination-city Wikipedia pages instead of AI/pharma/EV entities.

name: longtrends
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python package (16 stars, updated 5 Jun 2026) specifically built to download and stitch together LONG-TERM Google Trends series — overlapping-window rescaling to overcome Google's short per-request lookback and resampling instability, producing one continuous multi-year daily/weekly index per keyword.
why_useful: Same problem class as gtab (comparability of Trends magnitudes over long windows) but via overlapping-window rescaling rather than anchor-bank calibration; a second, independent method to try for gap #4/#17 if gtab's anchor approach has issues, and useful for reconstructing a longer historical Trends series for travel/Airbnb-adjacent terms than our current 9-term pull.
time_coverage: as long as Google Trends itself goes back (2004+), reconstructed
themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
why_all: Same problem class as gtab (comparability of Trends magnitudes over long windows) but via overlapping-window rescaling rather than anchor-bank calibration; a second, independent method to try for gap #4/#17 if gtab's anchor approach has issues, and useful for reconstructing a longer historical Trends series for travel/Airbnb-adjacent terms than our current 9-term pull.

Cheap, minimal-dependency way to get a longer, internally-consistent history for any travel/ABNB-adjacent search term (gap #4: historical/point-in-time trends), complementary to gtab (which calibrates absolute level rather than just stitching length).

name: GoogleTrends-Scraper
what_it_holds: Python implementation (226 stars, updated 2 Sep 2026) for scraping DAILY Google Trends data over long time periods by chaining overlapping weekly/monthly pulls and rescaling — same genre as longtrends, more actively maintained and higher-starred.
why_useful: Alternative, more popular long-history daily Trends reconstruction method; relevant to gap #4 (historical Trends with pull dates, if run and logged repeatedly) and gap #17 (mixed-frequency nowcasting inputs need daily rather than weekly granularity).
themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
why_all: Alternative, more popular long-history daily Trends reconstruction method; relevant to gap #4 (historical Trends with pull dates, if run and logged repeatedly) and gap #17 (mixed-frequency nowcasting inputs need daily rather than weekly granularity).

name: trendspyg
what_it_holds: Actively maintained Python library + CLI (successor-style to pytrends, now that pytrends is archived) for interest-over-time, interest-by-region, related queries, and multi-property (YouTube/News/Images/Shopping) Trends data. New in v1.3.0: opt-in local SQLite archiving so repeated fetches build a self-owned historical/point-in-time snapshot store going forward (cannot backfill past data Google no longer serves). MIT license, v1.8.0, 50 stars/7 forks, active development.
why_useful: Google periodically breaks the endpoints pytrends scrapes; having a maintained alternative reduces operational risk for the weekly Trends re-pull mentioned in team memory notes. No new data, purely a resilience/tooling candidate.
duplicate_of_holding: functional duplicate of pytrends, actively maintained fallback
themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
why_all: Google periodically breaks the endpoints pytrends scrapes; having a maintained alternative reduces operational risk for the weekly Trends re-pull mentioned in team memory notes. No new data, purely a resilience/tooling candidate.
Practical tool for building a going-forward point-in-time Trends vintage register (gap #4) cheaply, and a maintained replacement now that the original pytrends is archived/read-only.
